brief: For private-sector CZ banking and payments awards, the vendor side is usually the only public trace, and this pass confirms the pattern is real and productive: Diebold Nixdorf publishes a fully named ČSOB case study (whole ATM estate, ~200 DN Series recyclers, end-to-end outsourcing) that no register would ever carry, Asseco CE maintains a Czech-language reference list of CZ banks and building societies, and KB SmartPay documents the Komerční banka–Worldline acquiring alliance. The landscape splits into four usable layers: OEM/global-vendor newsrooms and case-study indexes (Diebold, NCR Atleos, Auriga, Thales, Worldline), Czech integrator news and 'reference/případové studie' pages (Cleverlance, Enehano, Printec, Monet+), Czech-language aggregation and republication feeds that surface those claims faster than the vendors' own sites (bankovnictvionline.cz, penize.cz/tiskove-zpravy, kurzy.cz, systemonline.cz vendor-bylined articles), and an entity/corroboration layer (bank press rooms, IČO register mirrors, LEI) for confirming and dating a claim. The main weaknesses are that global platform vendors (Temenos, Backbase, Fiserv, Thales) name no Czech customers publicly, several key CZ vendors including Monet+ and Printec CZ have no discoverable local reference page, and the retail half of this cell — self-checkout and POS wins at Czech chains — remains entirely uncovered and should be the next pass.
